newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Light Australian stocks stand still at open.
newsitem.headline: Light Australian stocks stand still at open.

text.p: A lightly traded Australian share market stood still at the open on Tuesday with little guidance from offshore markets and no clear direction seen.
The All Ordinaries index added just 0.1 points to 2,706.1.
"It's going to be a bit of a quiet day unless something out of the ordinary pops up. The Dow didn't do much and gold didn't either," said Jim Tredenick, senior dealer at Nevitts Ltd.
The attention turned to individual stocks with a broader impetus lacking.
Jeans retailer Just Jeans Holdings dropped 7.4 percent to A$1.50 (US$1.11), their lowest level since October 1993, following a profit warning after the close of trading on Monday.

The company said pre-tax profit would be 65 percent lower in the year to end-July than in the previous corresponding period. It cited poor merchandise decisions combined with exceptionally difficult apparel retailing conditions for the earnings slump.
Nickel producer QNI shed 6.4 percent to A$2.34 after releasing the report on its Gencor merger plan.
QNI said an independent expert's report had found the deal to be fair and reasonable.
Under the deal, QNI is to issue 455.8 million new shares to Gencor's base metals arm Billiton Plc, representing 52.5 percent of the enlarged QNI.
The capital return to shareholders would be 30 cents per share, compared with 28 cents previously.
Initial views on the deal in June saw the merger as much more favourable to Gencor, with QNI said to be paying too much for assets it acquired from Gencor.
"It still appears to be a better deal for Gencor than QNI," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about six to five, while about 44 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
